name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
history: Polish immigrants on Syracuse's Westside petitioned for their own parish, founded in 1892. The congregation outgrew its first church within a decade; parishioners dug and built the foundations of the new one themselves to save money. It was completed and dedicated in 1910 by Bishop Paul Peter Rhode. It was named a basilica in 1998.
arch: A cruciform Gothic Revival church in stone with marble veneer by Syracuse architects Merrick and Randall. Its two spires reach 212 feet.
features: Its stained glass comes from Munich, the Henry Keck studio in Syracuse, and St. Louis.
One window shows St. Maximilian Kolbe, the Polish priest killed at Auschwitz.

look.d: The twin spires are the tallest on Syracuse's Westside.
A window honours the Polish martyr of Auschwitz.

fun: A 1927 Skinner organ from a closed downtown church was moved here to replace the 1910 organ.
journal: Parishioners poured their own foundations. The spires went up 212 feet.
